name: strangle_mgmt
claim: Sell 16-20 delta strangles at 45-60 DTE and manage at 50% of max profit or ~21 DTE
tasty_value: Sell strangles around 45 DTE at about 16 delta; take profit at 50% of the credit or manage at about 21 DTE
tasty_note: Filled in Phase 02 (2026-10-25) from tastylive pages and checked episode extracts.
our_value: Managed 16-delta 45-DTE strangle (model): win rate 87%, mean +0.26 credits/trade, mean credit 1.15% of notional, CVaR(5%) -3.01 credits, worst -28.8 credits; mean return on Reg-T BPR +2.74% per trade; worst book year 2018 (-4.0% of notional).
data: Yahoo ^GSPC close, ^VIX close, ^IRX (daily); no option quotes
method: Every trading day: sell a 16-delta put and 16-delta call at 45 DTE (also 30 and 60), strikes and marks from Black-Scholes with sigma = that day's VIX, r = ^IRX, no dividends, marked at each close; exits per rule at the close that triggers. P&L per 1x SPX notional; 'credits' = P&L / entry credit. 'Book' = one strangle at a time, the next opened at the exit close, P&L summed per year in % of notional. BPR = approximate Reg T (15% of underlying less OTM, min 10%, plus premium).
caveats: Illustrative only: no skew (real 16-delta puts trade several vol points above VIX and calls below), so the put credit and the size of crash losses are understated and the call side is overstated.
No real quotes, no bid-ask, no commissions; marks at closes only, so intraday gaps and stop slippage (Feb 2018) are missed.
One flat VIX for all strikes and remaining tenors; VIX is 30-day, so 60-DTE pricing and the tenor comparison are rough.
Strikes are not rounded to the SPX grid; expiry on the last trading day on/before entry + DTE; no early assignment (SPX is European).
Daily entries overlap heavily; trade counts overstate independent observations.
No dividends in the forward, which slightly misplaces strikes (~0.2% at 45 DTE).

claims.text: Sell 16-20 delta strangles at 45-60 DTE and manage at 50% of max profit or ~21 DTE
claims.tasty_value: Sell strangles around 45 DTE at about 16 delta; take profit at 50% of the credit or manage at about 21 DTE
claims.tasty_note: Filled in Phase 02 (2026-10-25) from tastylive pages and checked episode extracts.
claims.our_value: Managed 16-delta 45-DTE strangle (model): win rate 87%, mean +0.26 credits/trade, mean credit 1.15% of notional, CVaR(5%) -3.01 credits, worst -28.8 credits; mean return on Reg-T BPR +2.74% per trade; worst book year 2018 (-4.0% of notional).

claims.text: Managing winners at 50% of max profit improves results
claims.tasty_value: Close winners at about 50% of max profit: higher win rate, capital freed to redeploy, better P&L per day
claims.tasty_note: The managing-winners page gives no resulting figure.
claims.our_value: 50% target vs hold: win rate 96% vs 92%; mean P&L +0.36 vs +0.64 credits per trade; P&L/day +2.04 vs +1.69 bp of notional; one-at-a-time book +6.93% vs +5.83% of notional a year.

claims.text: Exiting at 21 DTE reduces tail losses
claims.tasty_value: Closing at 21 DTE cut the worst-5% loss by 46% in SPY and 40-60% across four ETFs vs holding (2006-2023)
claims.tasty_note: tastylive's figure is larger than our model's (about a third).
claims.our_value: 21-DTE exit vs hold: CVaR(5%) -3.09 vs -4.69 credits (-3.46% vs -5.12% of notional); max loss -28.8 vs -29.4 credits; stdev 1.25% vs 1.80%.

claims.text: Management rules increase the strategy's expected edge
claims.tasty_value: Managing early (50% or 21 DTE) at about 45 DTE gave the best results in both high and low IV; early profit-taking described as an advantage beyond the volatility premium
claims.tasty_note: Measured on win rate, standard deviation and return on buying power, not on expected edge per unit of risk.
claims.our_value: 50%-or-21-DTE vs hold: mean P&L per trade +0.319% vs +0.750% of notional; one-at-a-time book +5.84% vs +5.83% a year (20 vs 8 trades/yr).

claims.text: Avoid hard stop-losses on short premium
claims.tasty_value: Close a losing premium-selling trade at a net loss of 2x the credit received (described as optimal in tastylive research)
claims.tasty_note: Note the tension: the claim says 'avoid hard stops', while this tastylive page recommends a 2x-credit exit.
claims.our_value: Adding a 2x-credit stop: mean +0.21 vs +0.26 credits/trade, win rate 85% vs 87%, CVaR(5%) -3.11 vs -3.01 credits, book +5.62% vs +5.84% a year (closes only, so real stop fills would be worse).

claims.text: About 45 DTE is the best tenor for selling premium
claims.tasty_value: 45 DTE balances accelerating decay with enough distance to collect premium; lengthen toward 60-65 DTE when IV is low
claims.tasty_note: Filled in Phase 02 (2026-10-25) from tastylive pages and checked episode extracts.
claims.our_value: Managed P&L/day by entry DTE: 30 DTE +1.78 bp, 45 DTE +1.76 bp, 60 DTE +1.72 bp; book % per year: 30 DTE +6.25, 45 DTE +5.84, 60 DTE +5.75. VIX (30-day IV) prices every tenor, so this cannot see the term structure.
